images.title: Columns become a line
images.purpose: Shows each month's point sitting on top of its column, and the line joining the points in month order.
images.composition: A simple graph with four pale columns for April to July; a dot sits on top of each column and a bold line joins the dots. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A horizontal axis with four month names evenly spaced: April, May, June, July. A vertical axis with no numerals and no gridlines, titled '°C'. Four pale grey (#6B7280, light) columns of equal width, one above each month. Heights: April tallest; May slightly shorter; June shorter again; July shortest. A teal (#0072B2) dot sits exactly on top of each column, 4 dots in all, joined left to right by a bold teal line that slopes down. The April dot carries the label 'about 33' and the July dot carries the label 'about 29'; the May and June dots have no numbers. Exactly 4 columns, 4 dots, 3 line segments.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A line graph joins the tops of the columns in time order, so you see the change month to month.
images.description: Shows each month's point sitting on top of its column, and the line joining the points in month order.
images.context: Kerala monthly highest temperature, about 33 in April and about 29 in July, read approximately.
images.teaching_notes: May and June heights are schematic (between April and July) since only April and July are quoted.

image_decisions.why: The concept is the link between a column graph and a line graph; one overlay picture shows it directly.
